influences.name: The Band
influences.context: We played before The Band early on in Virginia. They had Billy Preston playing with them... They were one of the greatest influences on everybody—that entire era was.

influences.name: Garth Hudson
influences.context: At one point, when I was playing with Gov't Mule, we played in Woodstock, N.Y... I remember Garth in a wheelchair—just meeting him and not wanting to take up too much of his time. It was really one of those cases where I thanked him for tightening my view on what's allowed in rock music.

influences.name: The Rolling Stones
influences.context: These guys are some of the reasons that people like JB, Jimmy, me and Warren Haynes wanted to play in the first place.

influences.name: Grateful Dead
influences.context: It's like how I learned a lot of music history— I learned a lot from the Good Ol' Grateful Dead.

influences.name: The Grateful Dead
influences.context: Like the Grateful Dead before them, Panic developed its calluses and fan base through relentless touring and a swashbuckling improvisational approach imbued with multiple dimensions of sound and style – rock, jazz, country, blues.

influences.name: Col. Bruce Hampton
influences.context: Lead guitarist Jimmy Herring, weaned on jazz and the free-style tonality of Col. Bruce Hampton, plays faster than thought or instinct.

influences.name: Ken Kesey
influences.context: Cochran says the band, 'evokes a gypsy feeling for me, a feeling of the road that reminds me of Ken Kesey and Neal Cassady, that reminds me of the bus.'
